policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'he tarried longer than the set time' renders a verb of delaying; qere וַיּוֹחֶר and ketiv וייחר are orthographic variants of the same sense and the English cannot distinguish them. Base qere fallback carries the projection.

ASV 'and thereon was a girdle' renders a prepositional phrase 'upon him/it'; qere וְעָלָיו and ketiv ועלו differ only in the spelling of the 3ms suffix and the English does not distinguish them. Base qere fallback carries the projection.

ASV 'and they were gathered together' renders niphal קהל, the qere וַיִּקָּהֲלוּ; the ketiv ויקלהו (a form of קלל, 'they made light of him') would require a different English sense. The ASV wording selects the qere.

ASV text reads 'Cherethites', the qere הַכְּרֵתִי; the mapped textual_variant note 'Another reading is, Carites' explicitly names the ketiv הכרי as the reading not taken. The ASV wording plus the note select the qere.

ASV 'Sheva' transliterates the qere וּשְׁוָא; the ketiv ושיא would yield 'Sheya'. The proper-name spelling selects the qere. The alternative_rendering note ('Or, secretary') concerns 'scribe' and does not bear on this unit.
